call_points.text: FY27 capex guidance held at ₹750-900 Cr, with supply chain spend past its peak and new stores the priority.
The 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target is held, split half Domino's and half emerging brands.
Popeyes LFL growth accelerated to 45% in Q1FY27 from 9.2% in Q1FY26; management gave no normalisation level.
Domino's LFL was 2.5% in Q1FY27 against 11.6% a year earlier, on a high base with price increases taken.
A 200 bps cost headwind was restricted to 20 bps through price increases, waste reduction and efficiency.
LPG alone was a 120 bps hit; cheese, oil and chicken inflation remain in flux with more possible.
Gross margin was 75.5% in Q1FY27 despite the cost headwinds.
The Mumbai food factory was commissioned in March, with some part yet to be commissioned.
Asked for average order value, management declined to share it, saying only that chicken AOVs exceed pizza.
Management expects to add 230 to 250 stores in FY27.
Minimum order value was lowered from ₹149 to ₹99 to drive customer acquisition.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In FY 2015-16, Revenue Expenditure incurred by the Company but held to be capital in nature by the Assessing Officer (AO) in the assessment orders passed raising a demand of Rs. 23.32 Crs. The issue was decided in favour of the Company by Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in earlier years but Income Tax Department has raised tax demand on same issue in subsequent years and same are pending before CIT(Appeals).
tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company expects to get relief from the Appellate Authority and does not anticipate any material adverse financial implication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received final assessment order dated September 27, 2024 and date of receipt of order is September 30, 2024 for FY 2016-17 raising tax demand of Rs. 70.79 crores on account of certain Transfer Pricing Adjustments.
tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company expects to get relief from the Appellate Authority and does not anticipate any material adverse financial implication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received final assessment order dated October 23, 2024 and date of receipt of order is October 23, 2024 for FY 2020-21, raising tax demand of Rs. 215.97 crores primarily arising on account of mistakes apparent from records apart from certain Transfer Pricing Adjustments and other corporate adjustment. Further, a rectification application is submitted to the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer and pending disposal. The Company expects to get relief from the Assessing Officer.
tax_litigation.status: Update. The Company has received the rectification order whereby the tax demand has been reduced from Rs. 215.97 Crores (original demand - Rs. 216.19 crores) to Rs. 190.21 Crores. The Company continues to believe that the impugned tax demand raised vide aforementioned rectification order has been made ignoring contentions of the Company. The Company has already filed an appeal in the said matter. Post such redressal process, impugned tax demand so raised is likely to get deleted. The Company does not anticipate any material financial implications

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In FY 2015-16, Revenue Expenditure incurred by the Company but held to be capital in nature by the Assessing Officer (AO) in the assessment orders passed raising a demand of Rs. 23.32 crores. The issue was decided in favour of the Company by Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in earlier years but Income Tax Department has raised tax demand on same issue in subsequent years and same are pending before CIT(Appeals).
tax_litigation.status: No change. Post receipt of CIT(A) order, which has been passed, ignoring the contention of the Company, the Company filed an appeal before Income Tax Appellate Tribunal aggrieved by the order of CIT(A). The Tribunal has upheld the decision of the CIT(A), disregarding the contention of the Company and without providing cogent reasons for deviating from Hon'ble Allahabad High Court order on same issue in earlier years. The Company is in the process of filing an appeal before the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court and other legal remedies against the said order. Post such redressal process, the Company doesn't anticipate any material financial implications.

tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company expects to get relief from the Appellate Authority and does not anticipate any material adverse financial implication.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received the rectification order whereby the tax demand has been reduced from Rs. 215.97 crores (original demand - Rs. 216.19 crores) to Rs. 190.21 crores. The Company continues to believe that the impugned tax demand raised vide aforementioned rectification order has been made ignoring contentions of the Company. The Company has already filed an appeal in the said matter. Post such redressal process, impugned tax demand so raised is likely to get deleted. The Company does not anticipate any material financial implications
tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company has received a favorable order from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, which has held that the assessment order passed is void ab initio on the grounds of being time-barred, subject to further appellate remedy available with the other party.

tax_litigation.status: No Change. The Company expects to get relief from the relevant Assessing Officer and/ or appellate Authority.

tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company expects to get relief from the Hon'ble Delhi Court and does not anticipate any material adverse financial implication.

The Mumbai food factory was commissioned in March 2026, with some part yet to be commissioned.

timeline.summary: Jubilant Consumer Private Limited, Mr. Shyam Sunder Bhartia, Mr. Hari Shanker Bhartia, JE Energy Ventures Private Limited, Mrs. Kavita Bhartia, Mrs. Shobhana Bhartia, Jubilant Securities Private Limited, and Jubilant Capital Private Limited declared no new encumbrance on Jubilant FoodWorks Limited shares under SEBI Regulation 31(4) for FY2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,499.47 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹79.79 Cr.
Jubilant FoodWorks reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹2,495 Cr, up 19.3% YoY, with reported EBITDA expanding 23.7% YoY to ₹485 Cr.
Mona Aggarwal (MONA Digitally) informed that Q4FY26 & FY26 results conference call audio is available on the company’s website, May 20, 2026.
Jubilant FoodWorks received an environmental compensation order of ₹22.65 lakh from the Haryana State Pollution Control Board for operating a store without prior consent.
Jubilant FoodWorks hosted its Q4FY26 and FY26 earnings conference call on May 20, 2026, guiding for 230-250 store additions in FY27 and noting near-term inflation headwinds.

On its 13 August 2026 Q1FY27 earnings call, Jubilant FoodWorks held FY27 capex guidance at ₹750-900 Cr, reported Popeyes LFL growth of 45% against Domino's 2.5%, and said it restricted a 200 bps cost headwind to 20 bps.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for dividend at AGM

watchlist.response: Quarter-on-quarter variations are noise; annual 2-year CAGR is closer to 7% and delivery continues to grow strongly while MOV was reduced to acquire customers.
watchlist.text: Sequential deceleration in 2-year CAGR and delivery growth rates from Q3 to Q4.

watchlist.response: Short-term pressures exist due to energy and wage inflation, but structural levers like wastage reduction, mix improvement, and scale will help achieve long-term margin goals.
watchlist.text: Near-term margin pressures from energy, labor inflation, and higher delivery mix.
Domino's LFL growth within the 5-7% band
EBITDA margin expansion toward 200 bps target

watchlist.response: Management declined to give a normalisation level, saying it wants average daily sales materially higher
watchlist.text: Analyst asked where Popeyes LFL growth normalises from 45%

watchlist.response: Management declined to share the number, saying only that chicken AOVs are higher than pizza
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for average order value across Domino's and Popeyes

watchlist.response: CFO pointed to 12% standalone and 15.6% consolidated personnel cost growth, with per-store cost held down by productivity
